Definition: from the same as G40; properly, clean, i.e. (figuratively) innocent, modest, perfect:--chaste, clean, pure.
BiblicalUsage: In the New Testament, hagnós is the word for chaste, clean, pure. In Philippians 4:8, the text says "whatsoever things [are] pure." In 1 Timothy 5:22, the text says "keep thyself pure."
TheologicalSignificance: For me, hagnós is a reminder that purity is not prudishness; it is keeping ourselves for the God who made us. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
